topics.between_rounds_aside: THE HIDDEN SIGNAL. The interviewee mentions, in passing, the dead time between rounds or matches (matchmaking queue, loading screen, lobby, waiting to respawn, draft/picking phase, warmup) as when they actually talk to Claude or already alt-tab to check things. Never followed up: the next interviewer turn moves to a scripted question.
topics.control_a_overlay_covers_hud: CONTROL A (followed up). The overlay window opens on top of part of the game HUD (minimap, kill feed, hotbar, clock). Every time it is raised, the interviewer asks a follow-up that engages it. A correct 'missed' detector must NOT flag this topic.
topics.control_b_hotkey_collision: CONTROL B (below the noise floor). The default Claudictive hotkey collides with another binding (Discord push-to-talk, a game's quick-save). Raised in only 2 interviews, not followed up; a detector with a 3-interview floor must NOT surface it.

prompted_policy.prompted: An interviewee turn is PROMPTED when it answers an interviewer question or pitch about its topic, and VOLUNTEERED otherwise.
prompted_policy.pitch: A pitch or a leading question about a topic ('wouldn't voice be amazing mid-fight?') counts as asking about it.
prompted_policy.broad: A broad question asks only for what it names: 'what features would you like?' asks about every feature wish; 'what do you usually do with it?' asks WHAT, not WHEN, WHERE or WHY; an open question ('anything bothering you?', 'your favourite part?', 'anything to add?') names nothing, so what comes up in answer to it was volunteered.
prompted_policy.continuation: A bare 'anything else?' / 'what else?' continues the question before it: in the middle of the features talk it asks for more features.
prompted_policy.guide_s6: s6 (voice) counts as asked only where voice was asked about neutrally; a pitch about voice is a pitch, recorded under pitches.
